summary: This experimental RFC presents a generic connection admission control reference model and algorithm for IP/MPLS networks. Providers can use it to reject VoIP calls that would harm calls already in progress.

eli5.summary: A bus turns away more riders when full. This is a rule for a network to refuse new calls so existing ones still sound good.

questions: reject voip calls on congested links
how does gcac decide to reject voip calls
what parameters does gcac use for bandwidth
how does gcac work across multiple domains
subtitle: Bandwidth admission control algorithm for protecting VoIP calls in MPLS networks

tldr.problem: Service providers need a way to reject new connection requests when accepting them would harm existing calls, but existing MPLS networks lacked a standardized admission control mechanism to make this decision.
tldr.mechanism: GCAC defines a distributed algorithm that examines available bandwidth on each link using parameters advertised by OSPF, and computes whether a new connection request will succeed or fail before attempting to establish it.
tldr.outcome: The algorithm improves the likelihood that routes chosen for new connections will be accepted, reducing dropped calls when the network is congested. It is an experimental RFC intended for controlled deployment.

today: RFC 6601 is an experimental specification. Service providers and vendors may implement and test the GCAC algorithm to gain experience with bandwidth-based admission control in MPLS networks, particularly for VoIP services. The specification has not been updated or obsoleted.

sections.title: Admission Control for IP/MPLS Networks
sections.content:
When service providers operate IP/MPLS networks carrying real-time services like VoIP, they need a way to reject new calls that would degrade the quality of calls already in progress. Without such a mechanism, congested links cause degraded call quality for everyone.

The RFC defines the Generic Connection Admission Control (GCAC) algorithm and reference model. GCAC is a distributed function implemented at provider edge routers, core routers, and autonomous system border routers. It makes admission decisions by examining available bandwidth advertised by IGPs like OSPF, allowing the source router to compute a route with high likelihood that every hop along the path will accept the new connection.
sections.eli5: Before saying yes to a new call, the network checks if accepting it will make other calls sound bad. If it would, the network says no.

sections.title: The GCAC Reference Model
sections.content:
GCAC defines two main functional elements. The GCAC Edge Function (GEF) resides at the source and destination routers and makes end-to-end admission decisions. The GCAC Core Function (GCF) resides at provider edge routers, core routers, and autonomous system border routers, and makes hop-by-hop decisions.

The model uses Diffserv-aware MPLS Traffic Engineering (DS-TE) tunnels configured between GEFs based on traffic forecasts. Bandwidth is allocated per Class Type (CT), allowing high-priority voice traffic to reserve capacity separately from best-effort data. The GEF tracks bandwidth consumption on each tunnel and dynamically adjusts tunnel sizes when demand increases or decreases, using RSVP signaling and MPLS crankback for alternate path selection.
sections.eli5: The edge routers watch how much bandwidth each kind of traffic is using. When a new call arrives, they ask each router on the path: can you handle this without hurting the other calls? If any router says no, the call goes elsewhere or gets rejected.

sections.title: Bandwidth Allocation and the GCAC Algorithm
sections.content:
GCAC relies on each link advertising four key bandwidth parameters per Class Type: the maximum reservable bandwidth (MRBCck), the bandwidth constraint (BWCck), the reserved bandwidth (RBWck), and the unreserved link bandwidth (ULBCck). These are advertised by IGPs and available in the topology database.

The algorithm compares the unreserved bandwidth on a link against a formula that accounts for the aggregate sustained bandwidth (SBWi) of the new flow, its peak bandwidth (PBWi), and a variance factor (VFck) that models burstiness. If unreserved bandwidth exceeds the computed requirement, the link is included for path selection; otherwise it is excluded. The simplified version, used when variance factors are not available, simply checks if unreserved bandwidth is greater than or equal to the requested sustained bandwidth.
sections.eli5: The algorithm is like asking: if this new call comes in, will I have enough spare space left that other calls can still work? If yes, accept it. If no, reject it.

sections.title: Parameters and Data Model
sections.content:
GCAC defines parameters for each Class Type on each link. MRBk is the maximum bandwidth reservable on a link. BWCck allocates minimum guaranteed bandwidth for each Class Type. ULBCck represents the amount of bandwidth not yet reserved for that Class Type, taking reservation thresholds into account. RBWck is the reserved bandwidth already committed to the Class Type.

Additional parameters include SBWck (sustained bandwidth of existing connections), BWMck (bandwidth margin above sustained bandwidth to handle traffic burstiness), and VFck (variance factor, the ratio of the bandwidth margin squared to the variance of sustained bandwidth).
sections.eli5: The network tracks how much bandwidth has been promised, how much is actually being used, and how much spare room is left. This helps predict if a new call will fit.

sections.title: Deployment and Inter-Domain Operation
sections.content:
For connections within a single autonomous system, a source GEF can apply the GCAC algorithm directly to all links on candidate paths using topology information. For multi-domain scenarios, three main approaches are proposed: full topology advertisement across domains (using external NNI interfaces or BGP), MPLS crankback where intermediate domains apply CAC locally and signal rejection back to the source to trigger alternate path selection, and Path Computation Elements (PCEs) that execute GCAC within each domain and communicate across domain boundaries.

GCAC should be experimentally deployed in controlled environments like Enterprise VPNs or internal traffic engineering infrastructure, not in the public Internet. Operators should carefully monitor the effects before wider deployment.
sections.eli5: When calls cross multiple networks, they have to ask permission at each boundary. If any network says no, the call can try a different path.
